known_gaming.attack: Include multiple campaign names in a batch body and append an unrelated ineligible name; exploit overlapping/short entity phrases.
known_gaming.effect: The current per-candidate name match may attribute one body to multiple candidate rows; an ineligible item mentioned in a broader name can trigger a false positive or a broad entity list can satisfy several checks.
known_gaming.why_not_closed: No context-disambiguated multi-entity guard is included. Scratch reproducer: /tmp/automationbench-luna-marketing-20261004/sim_campaign_handoff.py; ordinary 'Q1 Webinar Series' and 'Partner Promotion' batch body demonstrates candidate fan-out.

known_gaming.attack: Send the ordinary batch more than once.
known_gaming.effect: A duplicate-send guard was tried and removed because it flagged the ordinary correct batch, including distinct candidates.
known_gaming.why_not_closed: The available join cannot reliably establish distinct same-campaign occurrence identity here; adding the guard would penalize a single legitimate batch. Duplicate detection remains a known gap.

known_gaming.attack: Create an email with missing or inaccurate facts, or omit the separate durable handoff document while still sending a summary.
known_gaming.effect: Recipient/content presence checks can still pass without proving the whole document/archive requirement.
known_gaming.why_not_closed: Durable document creation, complete source inventory and stronger entity disambiguation are not fully covered.

limitations: Current draft has not completed native replay/rescore/reload. Do not treat the simulator evidence as Luna replay.
